title: SIEM adapter requirements and conversion matrix
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures functional and nonfunctional requirements for SIEM exports (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel), the audit-log -> SIEM conversion matrix, RBAC considerations for filtered exports (RBAC v2), and operational notes for evidence automation. It's intended for security, SRE, and engineering teams owning connectors and customer integrations.

Scope:
- Export formats: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics/Event Hubs).
- Data sources: platform audit logs, API request/response telemetry, user activity events (RBAC changes, role grants, key rotations), evidence artifacts (attachments, redaction metadata).
- Goals: 1) Provide a single mapping that covers required customer fields, 2) Ensure PII controls via RBAC-based filtering and redaction, 3) Deliver guidance for on-prem/private deployments where customers host the ingest endpoint.

Target audience:
- eng: security-and-compliance, eng: observability, eng: private-deployments, customer-success (for requirements capture), and partner integrators.

High-level requirements (MUST):
- Delivery: Support secure TLS 1.2+/mTLS to SIEM endpoints; support retry/backoff and at-least-once semantics by default.
- Format: JSON-lines (ndjson) envelope per event for Splunk and Datadog; for Sentinel, allow JSON to Log Analytics API or Event Hubs wire format.
- Schema: Use the canonical audit_log_schema v2 (see sample below) and include stable fields: event_id, timestamp, actor, actor_id, resource, action, outcome, request_id, namespace, role_changes, change_details.
- RBAC filtering: Respect customer RBAC v2 export policies; connectors must accept a policy token describing allowed namespaces and event classes.
- Redaction: Field-level redaction hooks before export; support placeholder tokens (e.g., "[REDACTED_EMAIL]") and optional hashed fingerprints for linking across systems without revealing PII.
- Metadata: Include connector_id, export_batch_id, export_attempt, and s3-presigned-url when attaching larger evidence.

High-level requirements (SHOULD):
- Batching: Recommend batch size heuristics per target (Splunk HEC: ~5–10 events/req or 1MB cap; Datadog: up to 5MB payload; Sentinel via Event Hubs: use partitioning keys per tenant).
- Compression: Support gzip content-encoding for large batches.
- Observability: Emit connector-level metrics (success_rate, avg_latency_ms, last_success_timestamp) to Redwood Console.

Non-functional constraints:
- Throughput: Dedicated connectors must sustain 10k events/sec in Dedicated mode (configurable).
- Latency: Best-effort near-real-time (<5s from Redwood ingest to SIEM for hosted customers under normal load).
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, 6 attempts default, move to dead-letter storage after threshold.

Conversion matrix (audit_log_schema v2 -> SIEM fields):
- event_id -> event.id
- timestamp -> timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor -> user.name / user.email (prefer email if present)
- actor_id -> user.id
- resource -> object.type / object.id (resource.path when available)
- action -> event.action (string enum)
- outcome -> event.outcome (success|failure|partial)
- request_id -> trace.request_id / transaction.id
- namespace -> tenant.id / org.id
- role_changes -> change.role_delta (array)
- change_details -> event.detail (freeform, prefer structured key/value pairs)
- evidence_refs -> attachments[] (URLs or presigned S3)

Target-specific notes and samples:
1) Splunk (HEC)
- Mode: HEC/HTTP Event Collector, prefer token auth and TLS; support HEC compressed payloads.
- Indexing: Provide recommended index names: redwood_audit, redwood_evidence (customers can override).
- HEC Envelope example (ndjson per line):
{
  \"time\": 1697040000,
  \"host\": \"redwood-inference\",
  \"source\": \"/redwood/audit/v2\",
  \"sourcetype\": \"_json\",
  \"event\": {
    \"event_id\": \"evt_01H...\",
    \"timestamp\": \"2024-10-12T15:34:12Z\",
    \"actor\": \"alice@example.com\",
    \"action\": \"role.grant\",
    \"resource\": \"project:pii-migration\",
    \"outcome\": \"success\"
  }
}

- Splunk specific mapping guidance: map actor.email -> user.email, include event.action as top-level field for faster search.

2) Datadog Logs
- Mode: HTTP intake v2 with API key; support tags for tenant/org and connector_id.
- Recommended attributes: ddsource: redwood, ddtags: tenant:<tenant_id>,env:<env>.
- Sample payload (single event):
{
  \"timestamp\": 1697042052000,
  \"message\": \"audit:event\",
  \"service\": \"redwood-audit\",
  \"attributes\": {
    \"event_id\": \"evt_01H...\",
    \"actor_email\": \"alice@example.com\"
  }
}

- Datadog advice: use attribute flattening for nested change_details; emit tags for quick facets (action:role.grant, outcome:failure).

3) Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics / Event Hubs)
- Options: 1) Post to Log Analytics Data Collector API (HTTP), 2) Publish to Event Hubs (recommended for higher throughput/enterprise).
- Schema: Log Analytics prefers a typed JSON object per record. Include _SubscriptionId and _ResourceId fields when exporting from private deployments.
- Partitioning: Use tenant_id as partition key when using Event Hubs to keep order for tenant-scoped events.

Evidence attachments and large payloads:
- Design: Do not inline large evidence in SIEM payloads. Instead include an evidence_refs array with presigned URL + metadata (content_type, size, redaction_level).
- Customer requirement: default retention in Redwood is 90 days for presigned evidence links; customers can configure retention in Private deployments.

RBAC v2 export policies (notes):
- Policy token: connectors receive a signed policy token (JWT) from the control plane describing allowed namespaces, resource types, and field-level redaction rules.
- Enforcement: Connector must enforce both filtering (drop events not in allowed namespaces) and redaction (apply maskers per field).
- Audit trail: Emit a connector.audit_transform event for every transformed or redacted event with justification and policy_id. This helps SIEM detections know when data was altered for compliance reasons.

Evidence automation hooks for customer audits:
- On-demand snapshot: allow customers to trigger a manual snapshot export (e.g., for SOC review) that bundles events + evidence links into a single signed bundle.
- Automation API: expose endpoints to pull export status, request replays for a date range, and fetch proof-of-delivery logs (signed hashes) for each batch.

Operational runbook (connector owner):
- Deploy: Use canary rollout: send 1% of events to new connector endpoint, verify parsing in customer SIEM dashboards, then ramp.
- Failure modes: if SIEM rejects events with 4xx, surface to ops and stop exports after N sequential 4xxs until manual review. For 5xx, follow exponential backoff.
- Monitoring: set alerts for error_rate > 0.5% for 15 minutes, lag > 5 minutes, or dead-letter queue growth.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Standard for evidence fingerprinting/hashing across SIEMs (we currently have SHA256, but need format agreement).
- Q2: Should we provide built-in parsers/dashboard templates (Splunk/Dashboard/Viz) as part of connector package? (high value for customers)
- Q3: How to handle tenant aliasing when customers use multiple downstream SIEM accounts? (mapping table needed)
- TODO: Coordinate with APAC compliance for data residency rules for Splunk Cloud regions (ticket JIRA-SEC-1976).

Appendix: sample canonical audit_log_schema v2 (human-readable):
- event_id: string (stable id)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- actor: { name, email, id } (flatten for SIEM)
- action: string (namespace.action)
- outcome: enum
- resource: { type, id, path }
- change_details: key/value map (optional)
- evidence_refs: [ { url, content_type, size, redaction_level } ]

References:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SEC-LOGS-2024
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-1423 (SIEM export policy), JIRA-SEC-1976 (data residency)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connectors

Notes: this is a working draft — expect schema tweaks as we onboard pilot customers. Leave comments inline or ping #sec-infra on Slack for quick sync.
